newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds buoyant, U.S. to dictate next move.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds buoyant, U.S. to dictate next move.

text.p: *Australian bond futures squeezed higher across the curve, sparked off by heavy buying of the three-year bond contract.
*Early direction next week will be dependent on the mood of U.S. Treasuries after today's non-farm payrolls report.
Australian bond futures squeezed higher across the curve sparked off by heavy buying of the three-year bond contract, enabling the market to put in a strong outperformance against the dollar bloc.

"Buying of three-year futures dragged up the whole market. But it was difficult to gauge whther this was outright buying, like we saw yesterday, or if it was just shortcovering," said one trader. "This could turn ugly if the U.S. turns sour."
The U.S. releases its key non-farm payrolls report later today and the U.S. Treasury market response to it will set the early direction next week.
"Evidence of tightening labour markets will maintain the strong speculation that the Fed will tighten policy once again at the May 20 FOMC meeting," said Glenn Maguire, economist at Societe Generale.
Forecasts for March non-farm payrolls centre on a 196,000 rise after the 339,000 increase in February, according to survey of U.S. economists.

Today's local rally came despite data showing that the domestic economy continued to improve with February retail trade rising 0.8 percent when a flat outcome had been expected after the 2.7 percent jump in January.
Building approvals for the same month fell a larger than expected 3.7 percent, but was only a partial correction to the massive 10.4 percent surge in January.

"Private consumption and the housing sector have been two areas where the economy has been under-performing through 1996. Today's numbers continue to point to recovery in these two areas," SocGen's Maguire said.
Colonial State Bank senior economist Craig James agreed that the pace of growth appears to be modestly improving, but felt the overall economic picture remains patchy.
"Certainly monetary policy is firmly on hold and talk of tightenings remains premature," James said.
Key data for the local market next week will be the March labour force/employment report on Thursday, one area of the Australian economy that has yet to blossom.
The market is also hopeful that the Australian Industrial Relations Commission will finally hand down its decision on the national "living wage" claim.
The verdict, which has been talked about for many weeks, will provide one guide to future wages growth.

Local bonds made a strong outperformance against the bloc, particularly against Canadian and New Zealand debt. Canadian bonds weakened with their local dollar, which has been under pressure since the Fed tightened policy, while sentiment in N.Z. bonds remained negative after Thursday's sharp sell-off.

The three-year contract broke psychological resistance at 92.75, but now faces a congestion area from 92.85 to 92.88. The 10-year bond continues to make steady rebound from the 91.700 SYCOM contract low seen earlier this week, but needs to breach 91.920 to pull out of a bearish downward channel.
